proposed statement: The co-op has a seasonal operation with a specific timeframe for citrus packing
key statement: Bosveld Citrus packs oranges (Valencias and navels), lemons and mandarins for its member growers, from large commercial farms to small growers with five or six hectares, through one packhouse in Letsitele; the season runs from the end of March (early mandarins) to about mid-September (last Valencias).

proposed statement: The co-op has a process where grower payments are calculated using a spreadsheet that is manually updated
key statement: Sipho's spreadsheet has a row per delivery and is used to calculate monthly advance payments per carton of class one and two and per bin of juice, with a final pool payment once a year in February; payments go out via a bank batch file and the totals are journalled into LedgerOne monthly.

proposed statement: Bins should have a permanent label that can be scanned to track ownership without relying on cardboard tags that fall off
key statement: How will bins be labelled for scanning? Most bins belong to the growers, some numbered and some not; the co-op lends out about 3,000 of its own bins with numbers burnt in; Precious floated a clip-on plastic barcode tag that comes back to the weighbridge, and the consultant will look into what other packhouses do.

proposed statement: The weighbridge must keep working without the network to prevent trucks from waiting at the gate, which would cause fruit to sit in the sun for up to twenty trucks
key statement: Intake at the weighbridge must keep working without the network and catch up when the link is back; trucks can never be stopped at the gate.

proposed statement: The Optisort grader's data cannot be automatically exported due to locked-down computer and lack of password, making it uncertain whether the supplier can provide an API or CSV export
key statement: The Optisort grader's computer is locked down, its reports are PDFs and touching it would void the support contract, so getting packout data out automatically is uncertain and could slip; if it does, Marietjie keeps typing for a while.

proposed statement: The Optisort grader's data cannot be automatically exported due to locked-down computer and lack of password, making it uncertain whether the supplier can provide an API or CSV export
key statement: Can the Optisort grader's agent provide an export (CSV or API), and at what cost? Ruan will email them this week. If not, someone types the totals from the reports as now, or the PDF reports might be read automatically if they hold real text in a fixed layout; Precious will send sample grader reports.

proposed statement: The new system must provide deliveries and packout data to Sipho's spreadsheet for payment calculations
key statement: The advance payment calculation stays in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, because the board changes the rates every season; the new system supplies the deliveries and packout as an export.

proposed statement: The payment calculation will stay in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, and the new system will provide deliveries and packout data as an export for Sipho to open in his spreadsheet
key statement: The board's monthly report (volumes, packout, advances paid), which takes Sipho a day by hand, stays in his spreadsheet in phase one, with the volumes and packout coming from the system.

proposed statement: The weighbridge tablet may be stolen, so it needs a PIN or login
key statement: The weighbridge tablet needs a PIN or login and holds only what it needs (the day's deliveries and the grower list, not bank details), in case it is stolen.

proposed statement: The current system uses spreadsheets for advance calculations and statements
key statement: The advance payment calculation stays in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, because the board changes the rates every season; the new system supplies the deliveries and packout as an export.

proposed statement: Growers use a mix of smartphones and data plans, with some older growers relying on family members for phone usage
key statement: Growers' pages must work on cheap Android phones over slow connections without using much data, as a web page opened from a link (savable to the home screen), not an app to download.

proposed statement: Growers keep financial records for five years in boxes in the storeroom, where mice eat some of them
key statement: Deliveries and statements are kept for five years (the auditors' rule), including for growers who leave.

proposed statement: Growers should receive SMS notifications when their batch is graded with delivery details and a link
key statement: When a batch is graded, the grower gets an SMS with the packout (for example 78% class one) and a link; SMS first, WhatsApp perhaps later. Ruan thinks an SMS costs about 25 to 30 cents.

proposed statement: The system must be in English for statements and grower pages, with possible Xitsonga and Afrikaans for grower pages
key statement: Should the grower pages also be in Xitsonga (and perhaps Afrikaans)? English is the minimum, and statements must be in English for the auditors; the consultant will price the translation.

proposed statement: The weighbridge tablet must be rugged to withstand dust, sun, and gloves
key statement: At the weighbridge, a rugged tablet rather than the PC, with big buttons usable with gloves and a screen readable in the sun; at the tipper, as close to one button as possible.

proposed statement: Growers need paper slips for trucks to leave with, as they prefer paper over digital
key statement: Intake prints a small slip for each grower on the truck for the driver to take away; the carbon books stay as a fallback if the tablet fails, with a quick way to enter those tickets afterwards.

proposed statement: The weighbridge process involves splitting one truck's weight across multiple growers by the number of bins each grower has on the truck
key statement: One truck can carry several growers' bins (a contractor collects from six or seven small growers); intake splits the truck's net weight across growers by number of bins, and each grower's ticket shows his share. The contractor, paid by the growers directly, needs nothing from the system.

key statement: At the peak, 60 to 70 trucks a day, mostly between 07:00 and 11:00, carrying 6 to 40 bins each; 2,400 bins on the peak day last season and about 1,800 on a normal mid-season day.

proposed statement: The system must be ready before the end of February to support the first mandarins coming in at the end of March
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The tipper screen should have a single button for scanning bins
key statement: Packhouse users: two weighbridge clerks (one per shift, both together in the peak) and three tipper staff over the shifts, plus Precious and the foreman; the clerks are comfortable with WhatsApp and the WeighMate screen, the tipper staff less so.

proposed statement: Whether the monthly running costs include SMS services
key statement: The board approved up to R580,000 excluding VAT for development and up to R4,500 a month in running costs (resolution of 21 August). The financial year ends in February, so most should be paid, in stages, before then.

proposed statement: Whether the monthly running costs include SMS services
key statement: The R4,500 a month covers everything it takes to run the system, including SMSes and hosting; the resolution doesn't say.

proposed statement: The system must allow the weighbridge clerks to practice with made-up deliveries in February to prepare for the first mandarins in March
key statement: Training in February with practice days on made-up deliveries: two sessions for the packhouse team (shifts) and one for the office; a short manual with pictures; the consultant on site for the first two mornings of the season.

proposed statement: The weighbridge intake must be live by the first of March 2027 to handle the first mandarins
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The grower pages must be live by the end of April to provide statements after the first mandarins
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The system must provide a way for growers to see last season's deliveries for comparison with this year
key statement: The grower list with its orchard blocks and cultivars (about 600 blocks, partly out of date, checked by Marietjie) is brought over from the spreadsheet; last season's deliveries only if cheap, to be decided once the consultant has seen the spreadsheet.

key statement: Training in February with practice days on made-up deliveries: two sessions for the packhouse team (shifts) and one for the office; a short manual with pictures; the consultant on site for the first two mornings of the season.

proposed statement: The system must provide a way for the client to check spray records with auditors before the May audit
key statement: Do the auditors accept digital spray records? Johan will ask them; their next audit is in May.

proposed statement: The packhouse staff checks sixty batches a day during peak season, creating a bottleneck for the packout process
key statement: Does the grower see the packout straight from the grader, or only after Precious has checked the report (which would make her a bottleneck at about 60 batches a day in the peak)?

proposed statement: The system should send grower pages on Saturdays for the packhouse team to access
key statement: In the season the grower pages must be up on working days including Saturdays (the packhouse works Saturday mornings in the peak, when growers have time to look); an hour down is acceptable, a day is not. The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: The system should allow growers to phone the office if they cannot use the portal
key statement: A grower can raise a query on a delivery from their page, which reaches Precious with the delivery, scans and grader report; phoning stays possible, and she sees how many queries each grower sends.

proposed statement: The forklift driver cannot scan deliveries because they need both hands on the forklift
key statement: Who records that a delivery has moved into a degreening room, and where is it scanned? Not the forklift driver; perhaps someone at the room doors. The consultant will come back with options.

proposed statement: The client needs to add a UPS for the Wi-Fi access points to prevent network drops during load-shedding at a cost of three thousand rand
key statement: The consultant proposed that the tipper screen holds its scans when the network drops and sends them when it is back, as at the weighbridge: in load-shedding the packhouse generator takes about 30 seconds to start, the Wi-Fi drops meanwhile, and the access points sometimes take two more minutes to come back.

proposed statement: The client needs to track cartons packed per cultivar and class for the export agent, who requires this data by Monday morning to plan shipments.
key statement: The cold store (pallets with their own numbers, tracked in the cold store manager's book) stays out of phase one; the agent will probably want it later.

proposed statement: The client currently uses a spreadsheet to generate weekly reports for the export agent, which takes one to one and a half hours every Monday.
key statement: A weekly report for the export agent in Durban of cartons packed per cultivar and class, ready by 09:00 on Monday in the agent's template; the agent plans the ships from it, so late numbers mean the fruit misses a ship. Sipho now spends an hour to an hour and a half on it every Monday.

proposed statement: The client tracks pallets in the cold store using a sticker system with a book maintained by the cold store manager.
key statement: The cold store (pallets with their own numbers, tracked in the cold store manager's book) stays out of phase one; the agent will probably want it later.

proposed statement: The client's statements include packing fees, bin hire, transport, levies, and a comparison of previous and current payments.
key statement: Statements show the advance less deductions: a packing fee per carton, bin hire for co-op bins (R35 per bin per season), transport for the few who use the co-op's truck, and levies, with last month next to this month; Sipho will send a sample with a fake name.

proposed statement: The client needs to track the arrival of fruit from big farms via WhatsApp the day before, but small growers arrive without prior notice.
key statement: Big farms could optionally give notice on their page of the bins coming the next day (they now WhatsApp Precious), to help plan the line; a nice-to-have for a later phase unless cheap, and never compulsory.

proposed statement: The client plans to run the old system and the new system side by side for two weeks at the gate to compare the first month's export data.
key statement: For the first two weeks of the season the weighbridge runs the carbon books and the tablet side by side, with an extra temporary clerk, and Sipho checks the first month's export against the spreadsheet before paying growers.

proposed statement: The system should collect crop estimates from growers in February for the board's use
key statement: Growers can propose changes to their orchard blocks (cultivar, planting year, hectares) on their page, and the office approves them, because the spray records follow the block; today the co-op finds out only when the wrong cultivar arrives.

proposed statement: The system should collect crop estimates from growers in February for the board's use
key statement: Collecting growers' February crop estimates (bins expected per cultivar, which the board wants before the season; now on paper forms that Marietjie chases) on their page: in phase one if there is time, otherwise next season, priced separately.

proposed statement: The client needs to ensure small growers use the system to reduce phone calls
key statement: If the small growers don't use the portal, the calls won't go down; mitigated by showing it at study group days and with the extension officer, Mister Baloyi, who visits every second week.

proposed statement: The client needs to update membership forms to comply with POPIA regulations
key statement: The 2005 membership forms say nothing about POPIA; update them or send members a notice about the portal and SMSes before the season, with the wording checked by the lawyer member. Johan is the registered information officer.

proposed statement: The client needs to ensure the system is available during working hours for grower pages
key statement: In the season the grower pages must be up on working days including Saturdays (the packhouse works Saturday mornings in the peak, when growers have time to look); an hour down is acceptable, a day is not. The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: The client needs daily backups in a second location in South Africa
key statement: Daily backups, kept in a second location that is also in South Africa.

proposed statement: The client needs rugged tablets for the weighbridge and tipper with a spare
key statement: Hardware: three rugged tablets at about R8,500 each and a slip printer at about R2,000, shown as a separate line and probably paid from the equipment budget; Sipho to check with the auditor.

proposed statement: The client needs to handle potential merger with the Blyde co-op to support multiple packhouses
key statement: A possible merger with the Blyde co-op in Hoedspruit (about 60 growers) would add a second packhouse in two or three years; the data should allow more than one packhouse.

proposed statement: The client has lost about a hundred bins annually due to them being misplaced or misplaced in gardens with tomatoes
key statement: Tracking the co-op's own bins, about 100 of which are lost each year.

proposed statement: The client wants the system to be reviewed with growers before building to ensure it meets their needs
key statement: See the main grower screens designed first and reviewed with some growers before anything is built, and a half-hour progress update every two weeks showing working software, not slides.
